First of all install wine with the package manager of your distro. And while at it you might want to install winetricks as well as it is really very useful in combination with wine.

I will hardly get into play-on-linux here...this is more about understanding a bit how wine works. Still I recommend checking out play on linux as frontend to wine as it automates a lot I say here.

And one more notice about my laziness...a lot of this is copy&pasted from a comment I made some time ago on a certain other news aggregator site. Hope that is not too much of a problem.

Starting programs through wine is pretty straight forward...basically it's just "wine <programexecutable>[.exe]". Interesting here is that wine understands both, linux and windows locations as parameter. So a "wine /mnt/cdrom/setup.exe" is just as valid as a "wine "d:setup.exe" (given you setup drive d: in winecfg to point to /mnt/cdrom)

More interesting is if course how to install programs though the command line and what flexibility it allows you. There are for sure plenty of ways but I usually do it like this:

export WINEARCH=win32
export WINEPREFIX=~/winapps/someprogram
winecfg

The first "export WINEARCH=win32" statement makes sure I create a 32 bit windows environment. This is of course only interesting if you run a 64 bit linux and even then optional, but helps in some cases. It's a matter of experimenting if that one is needed.

The "export WINEPREFIX=~/winapps/someprogram" statement setup a new wine prefix for the program I want to install. A complete new wine environment is created in the directory specified there.

The final "winecfg" will then really create that environment and start the configuration tool for it. Usually I change to a virtual desktop in there (for better multimonitor support) and disable all the directory links in desktop integration so that all files really stay inside my WINEPREFIX directory and I don't end up with some directories in my home folder.

After that I usually install all needed dlls mentioned in the wine APPDB for the program I want to install with

winetricks

Important here is that this is done in the exact same shell as the export commands above so that winetricks will use my WINEPREFIX.

Once the WINEPREFIX environment is completely set up it's just a matter of running

wine <installprogram>

to install.

After installation the program ends up in $WINEPREFIX/drive_c.

For a first test I usually start it manually in the same shell that had my export statement above by switching to the directory it was installed in and running it with wine.

cd "$$WINEPREFIX/drive_c/Program Files/<program subdirectories>"
wine <executable>

If that works fine I have a very simple shell script template which I copy to ~/bin and then modify to work a start script for the just installed program. Template looks something like this:

#/bin/sh

# 32 bit wine prefix, comment with # if not needed
export WINEARCH=win32
# directory of the wine prefix
export WINEPREFIX=~/<prefix-dir>
# windows path on "C:" of the wine prefix 
WININSTALLPATH="Program Files/<install-dir>"
# name of the windows exectuable
WINEXECUTABLE="<executable>"
# optional paramaters given to the windows executable
WINPARAMS=""
# no wine debugging output fo performance reasons
export WINEDEBUG=-all
# nvidia stuff that is said to improve performance...just as example what else could be done here
#export __GL_THREADED_OPTIMIZATIONS=1


# check if we were started with a parameter
if [ -n "$1" ]; then
 if [ "$1" = cfg ]; then
 # "cfg" parameter so starting winecfg for the wine prefix
 winecfg
 elif [ "$1" = winetricks ]; then
 # "winetricks" parameter so starting winetricks for the wine prefix
 winetricks
 else 
 echo "Usage: `basename "$0"` [cfg|winetricks]"
 fi
else
 # no parameters so just starting the program
 # Changing to the install path as some windows program need to be started inside their install path and it doesn't hurt others
 cd "$WINEPREFIX/drive_c/$WININSTALLPATH"
 wine "$WINEXECUTABLE" "$WINPARAMS"
fi

Only needs adjusting of the variables at the start to match your installed program. After copying and editing just making it executable with

chmod +x ~/bin/<scriptname>

and if ~/bin is in your PATH you can just start your program with the script..or even start winetricks or winecfg for the wine prefix you created there (by giving it as parameter)

And just to mention it..I am terrible at bash scripts...this can for sure use a lot of improvements/fixes

Advantage of this is that you keep every wine program separated from others and can do whatever you want with winetricks, install any DLL you want..and it never influences other wine programs.

Also removing is easy again as it is mostly deleting just the WINEPREFIX. This needs one addition though...wine installs desktop files and mimetypes in ~/.local/share/applications. It's necessary to remove those manually...and afterwards run a "update-mime-database ~/.local/share/mime" to get rid of menu items and mimetypes for file extensions.
